# Tianhao Luo — Harvard PhD & Startup Founder

> Tianhao Luo is a Harvard PhD student in Biomedical Informatics and an AI startup founder. He works on AI for science, biomedical AI, and AI for healthcare — building multi-modal foundation models to understand disease mechanisms and translate them into clinically actionable insights. NSF Graduate Research Fellow (AI for Life Sciences).

## About

- **Name:** Tianhao Luo
- **Role:** Harvard PhD student, Biomedical Informatics — Harvard Medical School (2025 — present)
- **Also:** Startup founder — MedJourney and a stealth AI biotech
- **Focus:** AI for science, biomedical AI, AI for healthcare, multi-modal foundation models, computational pathology, spatial and single-cell genomics, generative models for biology
- **Location:** Boston, MA
- **Contact:** tianhao_luo@g.harvard.edu

## Education

- **Harvard Medical School** (2025 — Present) — PhD, Biomedical Informatics. Rotations with Omar Abudayyeh & Jonathan Gootenberg, Kun-Hsing Yu, and Faisal Mahmood.
- **University of Pennsylvania** — triple degree (summa cum laude) in Statistics (Wharton), Mathematics, and Computational Biology.

## Research (selected experiences)

- **Mar 2026 — Present:** Multi-modal foundation models for AI virtual patients — Mahmood Lab, Harvard Medical School / Brigham and Women's Hospital.
- **Dec 2025 — Mar 2026:** AI virtual cells using generative modeling — Abudayyeh-Gootenberg Lab, Harvard Medical School.

## Ventures

- **MedJourney** — Founder (Jul 2025 — Present). AI-powered voice-first companion for Alzheimer's patients. 1st prize, AdventureX. Meiling Scientist Fellowship (Tsinghua X-Lab).
- **Stealth AI Startup** — Founder (2026 — Present). AI-designed probiotics using generative models and microbiome foundation models.

## Professional experience

- **OpenAI** — prior role.
- **LiquidMetal Ventures** — due diligence on AI-driven drug discovery startups; expert salons at the Boston-Cambridge biotech hub.

## Selected publications

- Yuan, M., Jin, K., Yan, H., Luo, T. et al. *Designing Smart Spatial Omics Experiments with S2Omics.* Nature Cell Biology (accepted, 2025).
- Freda, P.J., Ghosh, A., Luo, T., et al. *Automated quantitative trait locus analysis (AutoQTL).* BioData Mining 16, 14 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1186/s13040-023-00331-3
- Luo, T. & Li, M. *Integrating Foundation Models to Address Batch Effects in Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis* (2024). Presented at MidAtlantic Bioinformatics Conference, Harvard Quantitative Genomics Conference, Rice University Gulf Coast Symposium.
